decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's established airfield lighting control business, Product A is likely to meet strategic aspirations well enough that a growing, hiring firm with R&D slack keeps it on the market.
Product B fits the firm's integrated surveillance and tower offering, and with no clear sign of failure management would likely retain it rather than trigger problemistic search.
Training services support the installed base and customer relationships, so even if results are somewhat uncertain the firm's organisational slack makes continuation more likely than withdrawal.

Because Product D appears to be a narrower standalone training course with weaker market prominence, management is more likely to judge it below aspiration and reallocate resources to stronger core offers.
Product E directly matches the firm's stated move toward collaborative, data-driven airport operations, so strategic fit and available slack favor keeping it despite uncertainty.
Product F is an advanced surveillance system in a technologically strong, growing business area, making it likely that management continues backing it rather than exits within a year.
